title: GPS ko kaise pata ki aap kahan ho?
hooks: GPS ko kaise pata ki aap kahan ho?
Kya aap jante hain GPS kaise kaam karta hai?
Aapka phone bina internet ke location kaise batata hai?
hook_why: Direct question addressing the core curiosity immediately, matching the channel's 'Kaise Tech' style.
metaphor: Invisible timing pulses from space forming a 3D intersection point.
mechanism: Satellites orbit at 20,200 km in MEO
Phone acts as a passive receiver
Distance calculation using speed of light

claims.claim: GPS satellites orbit at roughly 20,200 kilometers.
At least 4 satellites are needed for a 3D position fix.
GPS works by measuring the travel time of radio signals.

steps_learned: Satellites are 20,200 km above Earth (Space Segment).
Satellites broadcast time and position signals.
Phone acts as a receiver (listens to signals).
Phone calculates travel time of the signal.
Phone calculates distance by multiplying time by the speed of light.
Three satellites create spheres to determine 3D position (trilateration).
A fourth satellite corrects the phone's clock error.
missing_steps: The concept of the 'Space Segment' vs 'Control Segment' vs 'User Segment' (the three segments of GPS).
Why the fourth satellite is specifically needed for time synchronization (the 'cheap clock' vs atomic clock discrepancy).
The role of the atomic clocks on satellites that make this precision possible.
unsourced: The script mentions '31 satellites'—while the source says 'at least 31 operational satellites', the script implies a fixed number which is technically true but could be framed more accurately as a constellation size.
